Initial parsing suggests a single incomplete sentence fragment requiring extraction of the underlying rule governing dispute resolution autonomy.

Segmenting the clause structure reveals that the phrase denoting the dispute resolution timeline functions as a conditional temporal modifier rather than an independent constituent. Re-evaluating the verbal complement shows that respecting parties' self-determination operates as the core action governed by this temporal constraint.

Re-evaluating the noun phrase boundaries to determine whether the stakeholder reference functions as a distinct object or forms an integral part of the core assertion. Absence of explicit modal indicators confirms the modality remains neutral without mandatory compliance markers.

Initial classification placed the stakeholder phrase outside the core assertion based on prepositional markers, but syntactic context confirms it modifies the central noun phrase and belongs inside the core. Splitting the clause into distinct functional units isolates the primary conclusion from the preceding conditional modifier.

Initial suspicion pointed toward classifying the principle-style clause as a non-normative policy provision due to its framing. However, active verbs prescribing conduct align standard normative rules, overriding the policy exclusion hypothesis. Consequently, mapping the segment roles establishes the primary legal obligation and its accompanying condition.
